issues.on_page: Statement of Cash Flows - Proprietary Funds, Total: operating 191,637; noncapital financing (117,500); capital and related financing (155,260); investing -; beginning 714,042; end of year 632,919 (cash consists of 632,920)
issues.issue: Business-type funds are on the accrual basis and print a full cash flow statement, but proprietary was left null because the overall basis is marked cash. Defensible under the GAAP-only rule, but the data is there. The page itself has a 1-dollar rounding gap (632,919 vs 632,920; Water 3,253 vs 3,254).

issues.on_page: Fund balance - September 30, 2025 370,787; Balance Sheet p4: cash 366,569 + county treasurer cash 6,034 = total assets 372,603
issues.issue: beginning_cash/ending_cash hold governmental fund balances (366,860 / 370,787), not cash. This is consistent with the roll-forward the statement prints (modified cash basis), but actual governmental cash at year end is 372,603 (net of 1,816 payroll withholding liability).

The larger part (24,843, 63%) is intergovernmental revenue of the Fire department, likely rural fire / other local government payments, so the dominant detail category may be county/other local governments rather than other state aid. Marked review by the extractor.

issues.on_page: p12 Combining Statement - General Fund Departments prints the same revenue lines split by department (General/Park/Fire/Community Center)
issues.issue: Expenditures came from the more detailed p12 combining statement, but revenues came from p9 (which has budget figures). The no-double-counting rule prefers the more detailed schedule. Totals are the same (185,288), so this is a judgment call, not a counting error.
